title: TypeScript Library Rules
summary: Project rules for publishing a TypeScript package: exports map, bundled types, semver discipline, tree-shaking and tests against the built output.
description: Writing a library is different from writing an app, because every exported name becomes a promise to strangers. These rules teach the agent to treat the public surface as a contract.
They cover how the package is described to bundlers and compilers, what a safe change looks like under semver, and how to prove that the built files work before a release.
useWhen: You are starting a package meant for npm
An agent keeps adding exports without thinking about breaking changes
Consumers report missing types or broken ESM and CJS imports
You want a release checklist the agent follows every time
body:
# Project rules: TypeScript library

## Layout
- Source in `src/`, one `src/index.ts` that re-exports the public API. Anything not re-exported is private; do not add deep-import paths.
- Build with tsup, tsdown or tsc to `dist/`. Commit no build output.

## Package contract
- Describe entry points in the `exports` map with `types`, `import` and `require` conditions (types first). Keep `main` and `types` as fallbacks.
- Set `"sideEffects": false` when true, and list `files` explicitly so only `dist`, README and license ship.
- Dependencies are for runtime needs only. Frameworks the user already has go in `peerDependencies`.

## Types
- Enable `strict` and `declaration`. Prefer `unknown` over `any`, and never leak internal types in signatures.
- Export types with `export type`. Use `import type` inside the library.

## Versioning
- Removing or narrowing an export, or changing a signature, is a major bump. New optional features are minor. Record every change in CHANGELOG.md.
- Mark old APIs with `@deprecated` and a replacement before deleting them.

## Tests
- Unit tests with Vitest beside the code. Add a smoke test that imports the built package the way a consumer would.
- Run `npx publint` and `npx @arethetypeswrong/cli --pack` to catch export mistakes.

## Before finishing
Run `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` and `npm run build`. Report any change to the public API explicitly.

example.prompt: Add a retry option to the fetchJson helper
example.result: The agent adds an optional field to the existing options type, keeps the old call signature working, exports the new type from index.ts, adds tests, notes a minor bump in the changelog, and runs publint.

faq.question: Does this assume a specific bundler?
faq.answer: No. It names tsup and tsc as examples, but the rules concern the package contract, which is the same whichever tool produces dist.

faq.question: Why check the built package and not just source?
faq.answer: Most publishing bugs live in the exports map and the generated declarations, which only show up when you import the packed output.

access: Instructions only; nothing runs until the agent follows them
